messages.subject: Poor fit indexes
parts:

messages.author: 99a06696c483481a
messages.subject: Re: Poor fit indexes
parts:
This is not strictly a lavaan question. You might consider sharing this question on semnet, a more general list:
https://listserv.ua.edu/archives/semnet.html
The n.s. RMSEA is a good thing--it implies that your fit is not extremely poor. However, your CFI and TLI values are very poor, and the chi-square value contradicts the notion of the model "fitting well."
Why are you using GLS as estimator instead of ML? Their distributional and data requirements are about the same, but GLS exhibits some strange / nonintuitive behavior that most users will want to avoid. In fact, that could be a major factor in your CFA and TLI values.
If it were not for your choice of estimator, I would say that the issue is that correlations among your observed variables are weak, so that the null or baseline model (where all observed variables are assumed uncorrelated) is not as bad an alternative as it usually is. See if the choice of estimator has a major impact, but then examine the strength of correlations among your observed variables.

Dear Edward, thanks for your useful answer. I have already shared my question on SEMNET, and I received some valuable answers. Thanks for your tip. Do you mind, if possible, having a look at my model below?

Actually, I deleted the item Q7R in the model and the ULS estimator is the one that better fits the data. RMSEA value is not as good as it was, but both CFI and TLI suggest a better fit:

> mod1 <- '
+ EXTRAVERSION=~ Q1R+Q6
+ AGREEABLENESS=~ Q2+Q11
+ CONCIENTIOUSNESS=~ Q3R+Q8
+ NEUROTICISM=~ Q4R+Q9
+ OPENNESS=~ Q5+Q10
+ EXTRAVERSION~~ AGREEABLENESS+ CONCIENTIOUSNESS + NEUROTICISM + OPENNESS
+ AGREEABLENESS~~ CONCIENTIOUSNESS + NEUROTICISM + OPENNESS
+ CONCIENTIOUSNESS~~ NEUROTICISM + OPENNESS
+ NEUROTICISM ~~ OPENNESS
+ Q1R ~~ Q1R; Q6 ~~ Q6; Q2 ~~ Q2;
+ Q11 ~~ Q11; Q3R ~~ Q3R;
+ Q8 ~~ Q8; Q4R ~~ Q4R; Q9 ~~ Q9;
+ Q5 ~~ Q5; Q10 ~~ Q10 '
> Personality <-  cfa(mod1, std.lv=T, data=Datos, estimator= "ULS")
> summary(Personality,fit.measures=T,standardized=T)
